column1: # gate-monotone run against the ARMED build (local dev-patch, NOT registry) — validates the
# guardrail has teeth once the s6+ arms are live. Build: zenavif @ e7f39b6 with ravif dep
# repointed to ../ravif--statusmeasure/ravif (all 6 _LIVE consts = true) + zenrav1e master
# bc452b67. host=lilith date=2026-07-06. Cmd: GATE_MONOTONE_DEBUG=1 gate_kit monotone.
# RESULT: gate-monotone FAILS on the armed build (2 inversions) where it's empty on registry —
#   proving the teeth. Caught: screen/q80 s6 dominated by faster s7 AND s8.
#   Mechanism: fine_directional_intra is ON at s6, OFF at s7+. On the procedural screen fixture
#   it does 38% more work (1362 vs 986 ms) for equal-or-worse RD (s6 59.928 vs s7 60.086) -> s6
#   is Pareto-dominated. On photo it's only 3% overhead (469 vs 482) -> correctly not flagged.
# BUT the inversion is a PROCEDURAL-FIXTURE ARTIFACT, not a real-content bug (checked vs the
#   7028 (real line plot):  s6 53398/88.640 vs s7 54467/88.493 -> s6 has BETTER RD (fine_dir HELPS)
#   6096 (real scan):       s7 weakly better all-axes but only 18% faster (under the 20% margin)
#   q40 (all fixtures):     fine_dir HELPS (photo/q40 s6 62.732 > s7 62.617)
# So fine_dir at s6 is CONTENT + Q conditional (helps real line content + low-q; useless only on
# ultra-regular synthetic at high-q). NOT a broad encoder bug; the gen_screen fixture just
# over-represents the one useless regime. Lesson: gate-monotone's procedural fixtures are a
# COARSE CI guardrail — the corpus label sweeps remain the real validation of the s5-valley fix.
# This is the POST-FLIP envelope to pin at the dep bump (these 2 known fixture inversions).
